BiblicalUsage: Kilayim means two heterogeneities, two kinds that must not be mixed. Leviticus 19:19 forbids letting cattle gender with a diverse kind, sowing a field with mingled seed, or wearing a garment mingled of linen and woollen, and Deuteronomy 22:9 repeats the ban on divers seeds in the vineyard, lest the fruit be defiled.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mixtures are forbidden because God loves clean lines: His people were to look separate, sow separate, and keep separate what He made separate.
